subject: doc-examples gate: prompt detection keys on a literal string, so a lookalike glyph evades it
description: Chris demonstrated a sixth bypass of _tools/hexos/doc-examples.test.js: both the extractor (:91) and the anti-vacuousness promptCount check (:192) key off the literal 'hex>'. A <pre> block that uses a full-width lookalike glyph for a NEW prompt line, inside a block that already contains legitimate prompts, is invisible to both simultaneously, so the per-block coverage check passes too (the block did yield examples) and the counts still agree. He added a false claim that way and the gate reported 36/36, exit 0. Reverted, diff clean. Today's faq.html has no non-conforming prompts, so this does not affect the current pass. Fix direction: normalise the line before matching (fold full-width forms to ASCII) and/or assert that no line inside a <pre> looks like a prompt without being recognised as one. Worth doing given this gate has now needed hardening in six separate rounds.
